ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists published by the Department of Internal Affairs, OFAC SDN list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 designations, and INTERPOL/World Bank debarment lists. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, family members, close associates, persons from high-risk FATF-listed jurisdictions, or any sanction designation flag.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Register of Companies / NZBN Name Reservation Portal (companyoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or te reo Māori, using Latin script characters A-Z and Arabic numerals 0-9. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated consistently and must not be identical or almost identical to any existing registered company, overseas company, or reserved name. The name must indicate limited liability ('Limited' or approved abbreviation) unless dispensation applies. Names must not be misleading or suggest prohibited business activities not actually licensed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the New Zealand Companies Office (via the Name Approval System and the MBIE Business Services contact channel) citing the relevant sections of the Companies Act 1993 and providing evidence of consent, statutory authorization, or desensitization of the proposed name. For sensitive tokens, prior written approval from the competent ministerial department or statutory regulator must be filed. If the Companies Office maintains the rejection, the applicant may file a fresh application with an amended name, or seek judicial review in the High Court under the High Court Rules. All administrative appeal steps must be completed within the original 30-day reservation period to preserve filing priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are accepted for administrative and commercial correspondence, provided the company maintains a physical registered office in New Zealand capable of receiving service of documents and statutory notices. A virtual office address cannot be used as the sole registered office unless the corporate service provider maintains a physical presence, appropriate occupancy rights, and mail-handling procedures compliant with the Companies Act 1993.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Approx_5%_Annual_Probability for a pure EdTech subscription business with no physical retail presence. The New Zealand Companies Office, Department of Internal Affairs, and Inland Revenue may conduct documentary compliance checks, unannounced site verifications are rare but may be triggered by material inconsistencies, high-risk UBO jurisdictions, or adverse intelligence reports.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 10-19 (registration and certificate of incorporation), ss 31-42 (constitution), s 50 (allotment of shares), s 128 (registered office), and ss 131-152 (directors); supplemented by the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Tax Administration Act 1994. New Zealand does not issue a separate 'International Company' charter, so CK_IC is incorporated as an ordinary company limited by shares, with the internal IC designation used solely for group classification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, administered by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (NZ Companies Office online incorporation application, incorporating statutory Form 2 information).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up capital or statutory escrow requirement for a company limited by shares. Shares may be issued without par value and subscription consideration may consist of cash, property, or services pursuant to s 50 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED that the incorporation of the company under the Companies Act 1993, as evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies, is approved and adopted.

RESOLVED that the subscribers listed in Schedule A shall subscribe to the issued ordinary share capital of the company on the terms set out in that schedule. The shares are issued as no-par-value shares, fully paid by cash or non-monetary consideration, and the directors are authorised to allot, issue, and record the subscribers in the share register in accordance with section 50 of the Companies Act 1993.

RESOLVED that the registered office of the company shall be the lawful New Zealand physical address stated in the application for registration, and such address is hereby adopted as the registered office for service of process and all statutory communications until changed by a future resolution.

RESOLVED that [Director One] is appointed Managing Director, [Director Two] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Secretary Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each to serve from the date of this resolution until removal or replacement by the board.

RESOLVED that the Company Secretary shall complete all statutory registrations, open banking accounts, and execute all ancillary documents necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and availability search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online company name search portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a RealMe-authenticated search of the Companies Register to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing New Zealand company, reserved name, or prohibited name. If available, proceed with the online incorporation draft and record the desired name. No notarization is required for the name search stage.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
Directors' and shareholders' preliminary identity and contact data
Statement of intended registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, file an alternative name or submit a consent statement from the existing nameholder; the application may be corrected and resubmitted without a new statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitutional and governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal preparation under New Zealand Companies Office requirements; no government filing window is used at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution, or adopt in writing the default constitution under the Companies Act 1993. Prepare director consent forms, shareholder subscription schedules, and registered office address confirmation. Ensure the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand and not a post office box. Signatures may be executed electronically or in counterpart; notarization is not required for domestic signatories.
required_dossiers: Constitution (if not adopting the statutory default)
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Shareholder subscription schedule
Registered office address proof and authority to occupy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar later queries constitutional or consent deficiencies, file a corrective resolution and amended signature pages through the Companies Office; the company may also apply under s 24 of the Companies Act 1993 for rectification of the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application to the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online incorporation portal via RealMe authenticated director login
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online application for registration, entering the company name, registered office, directors, shareholders, and share structure. Attach the constitution and director consent forms. Pay the official filing fee through the portal. Identity verification is performed through RealMe; apostille or notarization of the registration instrument is not required.
required_dossiers: Completed application for registration of a company
Constitution
Consent to act as director
Particulars of directors and shareholders
Registered office address and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing within 10 working days via the Companies Office portal, correct the deficient fields, and resubmit; priority re-processing is available by contacting the Companies Office helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office automated registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the issued Certificate of Incorporation, New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and exact legal name as registered. Confirm the company's constitution and registered office details appear correctly in the online register. Download the electronic certificate and archive it with the board papers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN certificate
Companies Register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors of name or date, lodge an application for correction under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993 and obtain an amended certificate from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of first board meeting and adoption of corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and company secretary; no separate government approval is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass a circular written resolution. Adopt the first board resolution covering share issuance, registered office confirmation, director and officer appointments. Execute share certificates and establish the statutory registers, including the share register, director register, and minute book. Foreign directors may participate by electronic means if constitution so permits.
required_dossiers: Minute of first board meeting or circular resolution
Schedule A share subscription and allotment record
Registered office consent and address schedule
Statutory registers (share register, director register, minute book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If procedural defects are discovered, convene a further board meeting to ratify and amend the first resolutions; defective registers are corrected by written board resolution and backdated within permitted statutory parameters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, via the myIR portal and Companies Office data sharing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN, complete IRD registration for an IRD number, and register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the EdTech subscription business expects annual turnover to exceed NZ$60,000. Register for PAYE if employees are hired and for income tax filing obligations. This step is filed online and does not require notarized company documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Bank account details for the company
Projected turnover declaration for GST
Director and shareholder tax identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD query is raised due to incomplete information, respond via myIR with the corrected declarations; if a registration deadline is missed, request late registration and reasonable-cause penalty remission under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to a pure EdTech software and automated tutoring service. Relevant ancillary authorities are WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational health and safety and the territorial local authority for building compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no manufacturing or physical industrial operating licence is mandated for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 611710 digital services in New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) Te Mana Rauhī Taiao, New Zealand
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure software subscription service with no physical manufacturing, point-source discharge, or land disturbance; no resource consent or EIA report is required under the Resource Management Act 1991 national environmental standards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero in-house wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions. Cloud and data-centre service providers, if any, are expected to comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for electronic waste and the NZ Privacy Act 2020 for data-hosted residential and customer information; no industrial discharge thresholds apply to the company's registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a virtual or software-only office. If a physical premises is leased, a Building Warrant of Fitness (Form 12A/B) is required under the Building Act 2004 for fire safety and means of escape, and an evacuation scheme may be lodged with Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. WorkSafe New Zealand notification and a health and safety risk assessment are required under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake; online filing and registration portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz); export documentation interface via New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (Tradelink).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (IC) must obtain an IRD number by lodging Form IR742 (Application for an IRD Number by a Non-Resident Company) or the general company application Form IR596, accompanied by certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, directors/shareholders register, and evidence of registered office; Inland Revenue issues a unique 8–9 digit IRD number. If the entity supplies 'remote services' (including EdTech subscription software) to NZ-resident consumers or carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, it must separately register for GST using Form IR333 (GST Registration). The IC may also apply for Approved Issuer Status (Form IR483) to substitute the approved issuer levy for non-resident withholding tax on NZ-source interest. A non-resident without a NZ physical address must appoint a NZ tax agent to file via myIR; registration is completed online through myIR or by post to Inland Revenue, Wellington.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. The 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' classification reflects the IC's non-resident tax profile: it is subject to NZ income tax only on NZ-sourced income and is not taxable on foreign-sourced subscription revenue absent a NZ fixed establishment/permanent establishment. Available statutory mechanisms include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election (Income Tax Act 2007 ss HA 10–HA 20) for qualifying NZ close companies, conferring fiscal transparency; (2) GST group election (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 55), allowing grouped members to file a single GST return; (3) Approved Issuer Status (AIS) election to secure the reduced 2% approved issuer levy rather than non-resident withholding tax on NZ-source interest; (4) substituted accounting period election; (5) CFC attribution elections and branch-equivalent adjustments under the controlled foreign company rules; (6) hybrid mismatch rules (Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007) impose mandatory aligning adjustments and do not provide elective hybrid-mismatch preferences.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — value-added consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 turnover threshold for domestic and non-resident suppliers carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand (GST Act 1985 s 51); zero (nil) registration threshold for non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (cross-border digital services, including EdTech subscription apps distributed via Apple App Store and Google Play) to NZ-resident consumers under the remote-services regime, and for non-resident suppliers of low-value imported goods under the cross-border B2C rules — mandatory registration from the first NZ dollar of such supplies; voluntary registration permitted below thresholds where land transactions or zero-rated export supplies exist.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal API, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. e-Invoicing is voluntary and operates under the Peppol framework; GST returns are filed electronically via myIR on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycle depending on turnover; invoices must satisfy the GST invoice content requirements under s 24 of the GST Act 1985, but individual sales transactions are not subject to government pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under s 11(1)(a) of the GST Act 1985 where the supplier removes the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (extendable to 60 days or longer at the Commissioner's discretion, and up to 2 years in limited circumstances) and retains sufficient evidence of export. Services are zero-rated under s 11(1)(m) where supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, unless the services relate directly to land situated in NZ, movable personal property situated in NZ at the time of supply, or an obligation to refrain from carrying on a taxable activity in NZ. EdTech subscription services (automated tutoring software) supplied by a NZ-established entity to non-resident customers qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is non-resident and outside New Zealand and no NZ land or goods nexus exists; conversely, a non-resident supplier supplying the same services into New Zealand consumers is subject to NZ GST at 15% under the remote-services registration model. Input tax credits may be claimed on GST returns and excess credits are refunded by Inland Revenue, ordinarily within 15 working days of return processing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (Tradelink)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer evidence evidencing FX repatriation
Signed recipient declaration (for zero-rated services) confirming non-resident status and overseas location
GST return worksheet (GST101 or electronic equivalent) recording zero-rated supplies
Evidence of export receipt in the overseas destination (delivery confirmation or foreign customs entry)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rating substantiation documents, cross-checking customs export data, bank FX records, and counterparty residency. Where zero-rating is claimed without valid documentary evidence, the supply is recharacterised as standard-rated and the taxpayer faces a shortfall penalty of 20% of the resulting GST under s 141B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus use-of-money interest on the outstanding amount (currently approximately 8–10% per annum). Fraudulent evasion or intentional misstatement attracts a 150% penalty under s 141E and criminal prosecution under ss 143A and 148 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with imprisonment available in serious cases. The statutory time bar for reassessment is 4 years, but no time bar applies in cases of fraud or evasion, enabling retrospective clawback. GST-registered persons who improperly claim input tax credits face de-registration and recovery of all incorrect refunds with penalties and interest; exported goods not removed from New Zealand within the statutory deadline are recharacterised as taxable supplies, forcing GST reversal with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for conduct of financial services
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the IMF Article VIII. No exchange controls or restrictions exist for the repatriation of profits, dividends, capital, loan repayments, or trade-related payments. Companies may freely convert NZD to and from foreign currencies through licensed banks. EdTech subscription revenues received in foreign currencies may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted without any surrender requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts in New Zealand. Exporters may retain all earnings in foreign currency, hold them in offshore accounts, or convert them at commercial rates. The only compliance obligations are standard tax reporting under the Income Tax Act 2007 and record-keeping obligations under AML/CFT regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs (e-money institutions) such as Wise, Airwallex, or Payoneer are viable as supplementary payment processors for inbound subscription collections and low-value disbursements, but they are not regulated as banks in New Zealand and cannot provide a primary corporate settlement account. Their legal status is not recognised as an authorised deposit-taking institution by the RBNZ. They may be used for operational convenience, subject to the entity's own treasury risk policy, but core treasury and FX settlement must be conducted through an RBNZ-licensed registered bank to ensure regulatory certainty and access to local clearing systems.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident International Company, New Zealand registered banks generally require either a physical visit by a director or a video-conference KYC interview, depending on the bank's AML/CFT risk appetite. Remote onboarding is possible for lower-risk structures if the bank can independently verify identities and source of funds through reliable digital verification tools. A physical presence in New Zealand is not strictly mandated by law, but the bank may require a local registered agent or legal counsel to certify the company's existence, and may refuse onboarding if no genuine link to New Zealand is established. Strong legal and beneficial ownership documentation materially increases the likelihood of remote onboarding approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through trust or nominee shareholder layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified trust deed, full ownership chain chart, government-issued ID for all ultimate beneficial owners, and a professional legal opinion confirming the source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational or jurisdiction risk associated with offshore company formation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a valid Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of good standing, copy of registered agent agreement, and economic substance documentation demonstrating substantive business activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume digital subscription revenue without underlying platform verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit merchant agreements with Apple and Google, payout settlement statements, certified financial accounts, and a business plan describing the EdTech platform and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to jurisdictions perceived as high-risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide details of the counterparty relationship, commercial contracts, evidence of purpose, and enhanced due diligence files on each payee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of minimum capital or thin capitalisation indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a statement of financial position showing intercompany loans or shareholder advances, board resolutions approving the capital structure, and a tax opinion confirming compliance with the thin capitalisation rules under the Income Tax Act 2007.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders, including trust beneficiaries or parent entities, must be routed via SWIFT MT103 for straightforward wire transfers. The remitter must specify a clear purpose code such as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Intercompany Financing'. The receiving New Zealand bank will verify the source of funds and may require a source-of-funds declaration, supporting loan or equity documents, and confirmation that the funds originate from a compliant AML/CFT jurisdiction. New Zealand does not impose exchange controls on inward remittances. Funds can be received in NZD or held in a foreign currency account. For high-value transfers, banks may require pre-notification and enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for procurement, royalties, dividends, or operational payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, MT202 for bank-to-bank transfers, or commercial letters of credit (LC) for documentary trade transactions. For EdTech, the primary outbound payments are likely intercompany royalties, platform app store commissions, and software vendor payments. New Zealand banks offer API-based batch payments through the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) for domestic rails, and SWIFT for cross-border. All outward payments are subject to sanctions screening and OFAC-style checks in addition to the RBNZ/New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards with a licensed New Zealand bank for hedging known NZD/USD exposures
FX options (vanilla put and call) for protection against adverse FX movements while retaining upside
Cross-currency swaps for long-term intercompany balances and subscription revenue mismatches
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offshore where the New Zealand bank does not provide onshore NDF pricing, subject to internal treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation or the date of the last annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$10 per month or part-month up to a maximum of NZ$50; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to give removal notice and strike the company off the register; directors may be liable for a fine of up to NZ$10,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (total assets exceeding NZ$60m, total revenue exceeding NZ$30m, or 50 or more employees) or if it is an FMC reporting entity; a non-large private EdTech company may opt out of audit by unanimous shareholder resolution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 for-profit entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for Tier 2; non-large entities may apply the XRB's simplified accounting reporting framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing; share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and the resulting director and shareholder details are confirmed in the next Annual Return; if the company is an AML/CFT reporting entity, customer beneficial-owner records must be refreshed as part of ongoing CDD on material ownership changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-900 per annum depending on provider and compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500-10,000 per audit engagement for a small to mid-sized EdTech company; not applicable if the company is below the audit threshold and opts out

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% for all New Zealand-resident companies on worldwide income and for non-resident companies on New Zealand-sourced income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D Tax Incentive credit of 15% on eligible New Zealand R&D expenditure (refundable for qualifying loss-making companies); no general capital gains tax; full imputation credit system attaching tax paid to dividends; grey-list and active business income exemptions for Controlled Foreign Companies (CFCs); exemption for certain foreign-sourced dividends where the New Zealand-resident corporate shareholder holds a 10% or more interest in a grey-list CFC; loss carry-forward indefinitely subject to shareholding continuity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit; utilisation requires a 49% minimum shareholder continuity test under s IA 5 Income Tax Act 2007)
